title: EM9305 recover_stop completable: GPIO15 configuration clock and vendor event 04 FF 01 03
scope: Emulator-only changes in ~/Repo/g2-firmware-emulator (no commit). No hardware flash. NVM program/erase is not in this step.

gpio_status_bit.decode: GPIO InputRead3 (bank 3, pins 96-127), bit 21 = GPIO117, the EM9305 Ready line. Already modeled in G2Apollo510_GPIO.cs InputRead; no GPIO peripheral change was required.
used_by: context_check: timed wait Ready low then high, then event 04 FF 01 01
recover_stop: untimed wait Ready high, then event 04 FF 01 03

events.context_check: 04 FF 01 01 (word 0x0101ff04), already emitted on RESET deassert after a 1 ms functional startup delay
events.recover_stop: 04 FF 01 03, emitted only after the GPIO15 configuration clock reaches a functional enter-CM threshold

evidence: audio_ble_radio_wait_pulse_52e854 in display_ble_hci_radio_recover_pulse.c: g2_codec_pin_function(15, 0x183), then (duration*1000)/33 high/low pairs with audio_ble_hci_boot_delay_491102(16) (microsecond wrapper)
audio_ble_radio_recover_stop_52e8be: radio reset, then wait_pulse(40), then require event {4, 0xFF, 1, 3}
gpio15.pulse_count_note: wait_pulse(40) issues (40*1000)/33 = 1212 high/low pairs. The '40 pulses' shorthand in that finding is the duration argument, not the edge count.
gpio15.wiring: 15 -> em9305@2 in controller-peripherals.resc and the mismatch copy. Inferred from the recover_stop protocol and the finding above; not a measured schematic net name.
gpio15.threshold_note: Functional model, not a measured silicon edge count. 8 rising edges after RESET release enter configuration mode. Fewer than 8 keep the normal 04 FF 01 01 startup event.

model_behavior.clock_during_startup_delay: Startup callback enqueues 04 FF 01 03 instead of 01
model_behavior.clock_after_unconsumed_01: Replace the queued 04 FF 01 01 with 04 FF 01 03 so recover_stop does not first memcmp-fail the startup event
model_behavior.hardware_reset: Clears configurationMode and the edge count

firmware_verification.image: stock 2.2.6.10 stock.app.bin, PC 0x005E4233, NOR 69efc6d023779beec9dada757ec9fe852f9454b4b84bae6fe8421c703f35c9d1, controller word forced 00010304 (4.3.1.0 mismatch)

fd06.status: unmodeled; two attempts. Next gap is NVM program/erase, not recover_stop.

also_unmodeled_or_missing: Missing EM9305 memory fixture at 0x00F0040C, length 4 (update_prepare read)
firmware_verification.advertising: 010A200101 was issued. End PC 0x44adfa matches the earlier version-match stock 8s end PC. This is not a completed DFU: erase failed, and the stack still brought up the already-installed (mismatched) controller firmware.

app_dead_hypothesis.claim: The untimed recover_stop wait could explain openCFW-only app-dead temples, but only on paths that enter recover_stop, and only as a hypothesis until silicon evidence exists.
facts: recover_stop has no timeout: it pulses GPIO15 until GPIO 0x40010410 bit 21 is high and the event is exactly 04 FF 01 03.
Official 2.2.6.10 came up on the later-bricked pair, so on that silicon recover_stop either was not entered or it completed under official timing.

On the version-match sim path (synthetic-rf-trim-7 and a successful context_check), acquire skips recover_stop. The realistic post-official MAIN-only path is version-match. That path still does not reproduce app-dead in sim.
recover_stop is entered when context_check returns 5 (skip_read), when context_check returns 0 but factory trim bits [12:7] != 7, or later from audio_ble_radio_attempt_52edf0 (version-mismatch DFU).
app_dead_hypothesis.hypothesis: If factory trim is not 7, or context_check returns 5 on the real board, every boot including official would enter recover_stop. Official came up, so the EM9305 did emit 04 FF 01 03 for stock's GPIO15 pulse train. OpenCFW uses the same wait_pulse source, but delays run from MRAM (am_hal_delay_us / g2_norflash_delay_us_491102) rather than stock's ITCM-resident delay. If that changes pulse width or period enough that the EM9305 never enters CM, recover_stop never sees 04 FF 01 03 and hangs until the watchdog — no advertising, no case frame, matching the brick. This is residual (iii).
app_dead_hypothesis.not_proven: No factory trim dump and no GPIO15 traces. The sim trim-7 fixture hides the trim-mismatch acquire path. Do not treat this as the established brick cause.

next: Implement EM9305 NVM program/erase (HCI 0xFD06 EMSMM_NVMEraseMain first), then the remaining recover/reconfigure/finalize commands, include g2.reset in the mismatch pair, and re-run through a completed DFU. Then (3) case-reply disarm with a pogo product-test frame.
